The '''1958–59 season''' was Real Madrid Club de Fútbol's 56th season in existence and the club's 28th consecutive season in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
During the summer Hungarian player [[Ferenc Puskás]] arrived to the club<ref>{{cite news|title=Ferenc Puskas, 79, International Soccer Star, Dies|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/11/18/sports/soccer/18puskas.html?_r=1&oref=slogin|accessdate=8 March 2008|first=Jack|last=Bell|date=18 November 2006}}</ref> after a two-year FIFA ban on him due to his defection from communist Hungary.<ref>Puskas did not return to Budapest after the Soviet repression of the [[1956 Hungarian Revolution]]. {{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/nov/17/newsstory.sport8|work=The Guardian|author=Brian Glanville|title= Ferenc Puskas}}</ref> The move was controversial due to the player's age (31 years old) and him allegedly being overweight, the reasons why he had been already turned down by Juventus, Milan,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=591759&cc=5901|title=Puskas, the Galloping Major|publisher=ESPN FC|accessdate=27 February 2016|archive-date=21 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121021224131/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=591759&cc=5901|url-status=dead}}</ref> and Manchester United.

However, Puskas and Di Stefano completed a lethal duo with an astonishing campaign collecting the club's fourth consecutive [[1959 European Cup Final|European Cup]], defeating [[Just Fontaine]]'s [[Stade de Reims]]. However, Puskas missed the final match due to a technical decision by head coach [[Luis Carniglia]], who was fired after that by club chairman Santiago Bernabéu.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ferenc Puskas, 79, International Soccer Star, Dies|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/11/18/sports/soccer/18puskas.html?_r=1&oref=slogin|accessdate=8 March 2008|first=Jack|last=Bell|date=18 November 2006}}</ref> Additionally, Di Stefano clinched another top scorer individual trophy in the Spanish league with 23 goals. Puskas was second with 21 goals.

The squad finished in a decent second spot in the league standings, four points behind champions [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], despite scoring a club record 89 goals (to Barcelona's 96). In June, Real Madrid reached the semi-finals of [[1958–59 Copa del Generalísimo|Copa del Generalísimo]], where they were defeated by Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spancup1959.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|title=Spanish Cup 1959}}</ref>
